comparison.objective: Draw a 9–11 ml liquid dose from a vial into a syringe and return the syringe to its rack; candidate iteratively tunes and locks a shock absorber for safe robot-axis stopping.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1095 requires needle alignment/insertion, one-hand syringe stabilization, coordinated plunger pulling, extraction, and precise rack replacement. Candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, captive-setscrew unlocking, collar counterholding and fine rotation, tool reacquisition, bounded relocking torque, and observation-driven adjustment.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1095 requires 9–11 ml liquid, at most 1 ml air, needle removal, upright rack placement, release, and arm return. Candidate requires two physical impacts meeting stroke, energy, velocity, rebound, overload, hard-stop, and post-lock drift constraints.
comparison.reason: Although both use bimanual stabilization and precise axial manipulation, dose metering through syringe/plunger motion tests a different mechanism and outcome from tuning, locking, and validating dynamic energy absorption.
